There is a church in the University District of Seattle that has allowed an African festival the use of one of its meeting rooms, and, as I write this, there is a deafening ugly noise of Africans screeching and non-stop thumping and scraping, which is the sound of the recorded voodoo trance music played at top volume, and since the alley door is wide open, and I live directly across the alley from this cacaphony, it is getting on my nerves. It was the same last night, and it occurred to me that it is odd and troubling that I would just take these alien emanations in stride without at least investigating further. So, moments ago, I appeared in the doorway and asked what was going on. A negro dressed in an orange and black native costume informed me that it is an "African Cultural festival," and that it is "open to the public." So, out of sheer morbid curiosity, I actually took a peek into the room, which was wall-to-wall sheboons, all dressed in matching orange and black dresses and headdresses, doing the voodoo butt dance routine, and they were all grinning like apes. It was surreal, and it was clear that the black guy was uncomfortable. He was making crazy hand gestures to someone I could not see, grinning apologetically about the white guy who was on their territory. Bear in mind that the church in question was ostensibly Christian, and the people in charge saw nothing wrong with opening up the building to these foul creatures. I got the distinct impression that the proceedings were going to get increasingly more delirious, in the manner of voodoo gatherings, and that the phrase "open to the public" was to be taken with a grain of salt, so I left, and my windows are still rattling with the noise from across the alley. I am disgusted, but in this day and age, is there anyone in a position of authority in Seattle who would take me seriously if I complained about this? I seriously doubt it. Turning over a church for the use of a screaming afro-mob is like a feather in the dunce cap for the average Seattle liberal minister.
